subject: QBR alignment: release windows, risk triggers, and owner commitments
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR alignment: release windows, risk triggers, and owner commitments

Team —

We have the QBR exec pack on Sep 20. I need a concise operational summary for Product + Eng that covers: release windows (what's realistically shipping in Oct vs Nov), top delivery risks with explicit triggers (what to watch for), and confirmed owners for mitigations. Please treat this as an ask for the exec one-pager — one slide worth of bullets per area.

I've attached the projection workbook (QBR_release_windows_projection_v2.xlsx) with the model-level tabs populated from last week's estimates — update the "Final ETA" column and add a short note where there is any non-trivial risk. Also add rows in the Mitigation_tracker.csv with owners and target completion dates.

Deliverable: updated workbook + a 3-bullet summary per release area by EOD Monday (9/13).

Context for the execs: we want a crisp statement on whether the primary Oct launch window is still on track, and if not, what would move it back and by how much. If you see cascading risks (e.g., infra -> runtime -> model rollouts), call those out clearly.

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das | Sr. PM, Core Product
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR alignment: release windows, risk triggers, and owner commitments

Priyom —

Quick status after syncing with infra and runtime teams (high level):

- Core feature set (model serving API + routing rules): green. API contract frozen; integration tests passing against staging cluster.
- Runtime infra (KV cache eviction and autoscaling hooks): amber. We discovered a race under burst traffic that can cause increased tail latency — reproducible with our stress harness. Likely fix requires a small scheduler change and an extra regression cycle. Risk trigger: >3% tail-latency regressions in staging during 3-match stress runs. Owner: Marcus Lin.
- Quantization/throughput tuning: on track, but dependent on infra stabilization. Owner: Mina Haddad.
- Canary and fallback playbook: not yet finalized; need clear roll-forward/fallback metrics and a designated runbook owner. Suggested owner: Lauren Bishop.

I've updated Mitigation_tracker.csv (new rows for KV-scheduler fix and staged canary plan) with owners and target dates (KV fix targeted for 9/24, canary plan draft by 9/16).

Actionable asks back to product: please confirm which model variants are allowed in the Oct window if we need to fall back to lower-cost/quantized variants (this affects acceptance criteria for canary).

-Karthik
Director, Engineering

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jill Torres <jill.torres@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR alignment: release windows, risk triggers, and owner commitments

Thanks Karthik — good notes. A couple of clarifications from leadership perspective:

1) Go/no-go criteria: can we distill this to 3 top-level pass/fail checks we can present in the QBR? My proposal:
   - Stability: tail p99 latency under SLA (<= 450ms) during 1-hour ramp test in staging.
   - Reliability: no single critical infra regression open (severity P0/P1) blocking rollout.
   - Observability: core traces and cost breakdowns available in the console for the canary cohort.

2) Release window: I need a clear ask for the execs — either "Oct window: proceed" or "Request 2-week slip to Nov with mitigations". If we recommend slip, have cost delta and customer impact note ready.

3) Owners: please confirm owners for the three mitigations Karthik listed and add an escalation path if owners miss dates.

Jill — looping you in so you're aware of the potential timing variance; we'll call out any impact to your integration timeline if we recommend a slip.

-Lauren
VP Product
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudmarket.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 17:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR alignment: release windows, risk triggers, and owner commitments

Folks — ground update from infra implementation: 

- Reproducer and mitigation: we nailed down the KV eviction race; proposed fix is a scheduler guard that limits concurrent eviction+write operations. Patch ready.
- Regression/Cycle impact: requires one additional regression pass and a canary (2 days regression + 3 day canary on load).
- Timeline implication: given current sprint commitments, earliest safe rollout pushes the Oct window by 7–10 days.

Concrete numbers:
- If we keep Oct window and skip extended canary, estimated risk of intermittent p99 spikes increases by ~4–6% under extreme burst.
- Cost of 10-day slip: ~$43k incremental infra spend (estimated), and potential upstream schedule work for integrations (Jill, that could require shifting your test window by ~10 days).

I'll place the patch and test plan in the shared Drive and update Mitigation_tracker.csv with the exact regression dates. Owner confirmations: KV fix (Marcus Lin), Canary plan (Mina Haddad for execution, Karthik to approve), Observability checklist (Lauren Bishop to confirm requirements).

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Torres <jill.torres@acmehealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudmarket.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR alignment: release windows, risk triggers, and owner commitments

Thanks all — good progress and clear notes. For the exec deck I'll present the following consolidated call and ask for endorsement:

1) Recommendation: Move the primary launch window by 10 days to allow a full regression + 3-day canary. Rationale: avoids ~4–6% chance of p99 spikes and gives time for observability checks.

2) Go/No-Go criteria (must all be met to proceed):
   - Stability: p99 <= 450ms during official 1-hour staging ramp.
   - No P0/P1 infra regressions open against the release patch.
   - Canary telemetry shows no regressions and cost deltas within expected tolerance (<8% delta for the canary cohort).

3) Owners & deadlines (confirm by EOD Mon 9/21):
   - KV scheduler patch & regression: Marcus Lin — regression complete by 9/24.
   - Canary playbook + run: Mina Haddad — plan draft by 9/16 (done), execution completed by 9/27.
   - Observability checklist: Lauren Bishop — confirm dashboard + trace requirements by 9/21.

I've updated QBR_release_windows_projection_v2.xlsx with the recommended 10-day shift and the expected infra cost delta. Mitigation_tracker.csv now contains the tickets and ownership rows. Drive links below.

Jill / Samir — apologies for the churn; we'll flag the final confirmed date by 9/21 after owners confirm.

PRIYOM
Priyom Das | Sr. PM, Core Product
Redwood Inference
Attachments: QBR_release_windows_projection_v2.xlsx; Mitigation_tracker.csv
